html:
SMTO-EXE-0197 — SMTO lost contact with the computer handling your PDF

GUID: 3d788f06-602f-55a3-80c3-1436551b6053
Slug: pdf-gateway-lost
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO could not get a PDF result from the Gateway, the helper program that works with files on the chosen computer. Your original PDF was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway you used, and select Check connection. This shows whether SMTO can reach the computer that opens your PDF files right now.
  2. If it can't connect, make sure that computer is switched on, connected to the network, and the Gateway program is running on it. PDF work happens on that computer, so SMTO can't do anything while it is unreachable.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. If this Gateway then offers Update to a newer version, select it when no tasks are running on it. An older Gateway may refuse PDF requests it doesn't understand, and updating stops its running tasks.
  4. If you had pressed stop on the task, open Artifacts from this run and look for a new PDF or image before asking again. When a stop request fails to arrive, the PDF work may still have finished and saved a file.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds, and asking SMTO again for the PDF task returns a result or a new file under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and its Gateways. Don't delete the Gateway from Settings; that removes its trusted pairing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The PDF request to the selected Gateway was refused, could not be sent (connection or configuration failure), or a PDF stop request to that Gateway failed.

What this means

  • The PDF transport received a Gateway HTTP error, connection/configuration failure or failed cancellation response. The retained phase determines whether output publication was possible. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • The PDF transport received a Gateway HTTP error, connection/configuration failure or failed cancellation response. The retained phase determines whether output publication was possible.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original request, phase and expected output/artifacts; this category does not establish that reducing document size will help.

How to fix it

  • Check the selected Gateway in Settings > Setup > Gateways (Check connection) and confirm it is online; a 400/404/405/422/501 reply from /pdf/operation (failure_phase=rejected) means the Gateway rejected or does not support the PDF route, so update it to match the Server. If the failure came from GatewayClient.cancel_pdf_request (failure_phase=control), the operation may have completed: inspect the run's artifact workspace and any explicit output_path before issuing another PDF write.
  • Restore the selected route and inspect the original PDF receipt and outputs before another request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the bounded PDF receipt and input, reduce the request if needed, and retry only after resolving the reported condition.

How to verify the fix

  • The original result or publication state is settled on the same verified Gateway before new work.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
